title: Output flipping preserves bounded-error decision
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be a language of binary strings, and let $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. If $N$ halts within $T(|x|)$ steps on every branch for each input $x$ and outputs the indicator of membership in $L$ with probability at least $2/3$, then the machine obtained by flipping every Boolean symbol it outputs halts within the same time and outputs the indicator of membership in the complement of $L$ with probability at least $2/3$ on every input.
